_comment: What the node is made of, and where each kind actually lives.
This file answers ONE question -- WHERE does a class live -- and nothing else.
How to change a thing (the call, the gate, the proof) is docs/node/entities.md.
What to offer an owner, in their language, is node-versioning/capabilities.md.
One fact, one home, applied to our own documentation: no cell here is repeated
in either of those files, so there is nothing for them to disagree about.
JSON rather than YAML on purpose: the reader that matters runs on the node HOST,
where bootstrap/B01-core.sh installs jq and a bare python3. python3-yaml is not
installed there -- every `import yaml` in this repository lives inside a container
`registry` is ALWAYS schema-qualified. A bare table name cannot be checked: this
database has five names that exist in two schemas at once, and reading the wrong
one is how docs/node/entities.md came to name sn_config.flows as the home of a
workflow when the catalogue is sn_core.workflows.
Every registry below was read from a live node on 2026-08-16, not copied from
Row counts are deliberately NOT recorded: how many rows a node holds is
a fact about that node, not about the release.
_legacy_comment: Names that exist in two schemas. The `home` is the real one; the `twin` is not a
home and a checker must say so rather than accept it. The last two twins are the
dangerous ones: they hold rows, so 'does it have rows' confirms the wrong table.
sn_config.tools, sn_config.flows and sn_config.flow_versions used to be on this
list; B02 retires them when they are empty.
_classes_comment: kind:        table   -- a postgres relation in the node's own cluster
file    -- a path on the node; the registry IS the file
service -- another component's own store, reached through its API
none    -- real, and has no registry of its own
status:      real    -- exists in this release
gap     -- named by the taxonomy, not built; nothing may offer it
contract:    the bolded row in docs/node/entities.md that says HOW to change it,
or null when a class is not something an agent creates. A class with
a contract MUST have that row: tools/classes-check.sh fails otherwise.
This is the join between the two files, and it is not an exemption
list -- null means 'not actionable', which is itself checkable.

classes.note: someone OUTSIDE the business. People inside it are the user class.
a person inside the business; separate lifecycle from a contact.

classes.writer: core-api, and only for a proven session
classes.note: membership is sn_config.project_members. Real in the registry but not exposed in the UI.
grants are sn_config.agent_tools, whose tool_id references THIS table.
grants are sn_config.agent_workflows, whose workflow_id references THIS table.
the binding that makes it route is sn_config.agent_channels; the type alone routes nothing.
per-agent overrides are sn_config.agent_policy_opts. Absent 's seventeen; it is real.
delivery state is sn_core.message_state. Append-only, enforced by trigger.
append-only, enforced by trigger. Nobody creates one by hand, hence no contract row.

classes.writer: core-api /api/secrets, the only sanctioned write path
classes.note: sops-encrypted with the node age key. NOT a table -- entities.md said sn_config.secrets for months and no such table has ever existed.
cross-cutting; it is a comment on a task, not an endpoint.
machine output, deliberately OUT of semantic search. Nothing may offer this until it has a registry.
a short-lived work area that expires. Open question whether it is a class at all or a project with a lifetime.
No backup registry exists in sn_config or sn_core on any node. Backups are taken from OUTSIDE the node.

_filesystem_homes_comment: Class-home paths under /work, with the ownership and access rules the installer
applies via chown, chmod and setfacl.
writer_group is the grp-role-<capability> that owns the home. reader_groups is the
set of grp-role-* that get r-x through the default POSIX ACL. mode is the numeric
chmod applied to the directory itself; setgid is expressed here as the 2000 bit.
Four rows have neither writer_group nor reader_groups: _archive, _release,
_tmp and tmp. They are declared here
so the installer applies the mode explicitly rather than skipping them silently.
Per-project ACL rows for /work/projects/<slug> are computed at install time from
the project registry (grp-prj-<slug>, plus the `restricted` flag toggling the
grp-role-developer default entry). The base row `projects` is what the installer
Anything under /work whose top-level directory is not declared here causes the
installer to refuse with a named error.

filesystem_homes.note: Developer-authored monitors. Sysadmin reads for incident response.
Auxiliary tools. Developers read; sysadmin writes.
Owner-visible instructions authored by the foreman. Writer group tracks the capability (configurator), NOT the agent's personal slug: the foreman's slug can change while capability stays constant.

Transient staging. Every agent can drop here; nothing else. grp-agents is a collective (not a capability role) maintained by bootstrap/groups.sh apply_agents_group() -- every non-archived agent's os_user plus admin.
Short-lived work areas. Same access as /work/flows.

Base ACL for /work/projects. Per-slug ACLs (grp-prj-<slug>) are computed by the installer from the project registry; a project with `restricted=true` drops the grp-role-developer entry and keeps only grp-prj-<slug>.
Release artefacts. Writer group grp-role-sysadmin includes admin, which writes here daily. The directory must remain group-writable so applying the class does not block release writes.
Sticky world-writable scratch (legacy path, same as _tmp).
